context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability across disparate regional networks.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) using Mobile/Web Clients
- Licensed Clinicians using the Clinician Portal
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform deployed in GCP (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`)
- National E-Prescription Gateways (EU) & US Pharmacy Systems (HL7 FHIR)
- Identity Providers (EU eIDAS / US OAuth2)
- EU/US Regulatory & Auditing Bodies

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians -> Cross-Border Telehealth Platform via HTTPS / WebRTC (TLS 1.3) with regional Anycast edge routing
- Platform -> National E-Prescription Gateways & US Pharmacy Systems via REST / HL7 FHIR over mutual TLS (mTLS)
- Platform -> Identity Providers via OIDC over HTTPS
- Platform -> EU/US Regulatory Bodies via secure export API (HTTPS/SFTP) with regional data-residency filters

## Technology Stack
- GCP (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`): Regional deployment to enforce strict data residency (R-05)
- GCP Cloud Load Balancing: Regional edge routing pinned to specific data centers without shared global state
- WebRTC with TURN/STUN relay servers: Enables video consultations in low-bandwidth rural conditions (<300 kbit/s)
- GCP KMS (Customer-Managed Encryption Keys): Isolates encryption keys regionally to prevent cross-border key compromise
- GCP Cloud Storage with WORM bucket locks: Provides immutable storage for audit logs to satisfy AI traceability (R-07)
- HL7 FHIR and national EU standards: Ensures regional interoperability for e-prescriptions (R-08)

## Rationale
This architecture enforces strict regional isolation and cryptographic consent verification to comply with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR mandates. Regional pinning, immutable audit logs, and low-bandwidth optimizations guarantee data privacy, system availability, and regulatory accountability across borders.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict regional data residency, HIPAA/GDPR compliance, and low-bandwidth resilience.

## Key Elements
* Patients and Clinicians (EU & US)
* Pharmacies and Platform Administrators
* Client Applications (Flutter / Web)
* API Gateway (Envoy / Google Cloud Endpoints)
* Core Telehealth Service (Go)
* AI Inference Service (Python / FastAPI)
* Interoperability Service (Java / Spring Boot)
* Containerized SFUs (mediasoup)
* Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) (europe-west3, us-central1)
* PostgreSQL Databases with CMEK

## Relationships
* Client Apps to API Gateway via gRPC and HTTPS
* API Gateway to internal microservices via gRPC over Istio mTLS mesh
* Interoperability Service to National E-Prescription Gateways and US Pharmacy Systems via national formats and HL7 FHIR
* AI Inference Service to Cloud Storage via HTTPS for regional model artifacts and logs

## Technology Stack
* GCP (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`): Mandated for region-locked data residency and cloud infrastructure.
* GKE & Istio: Orchestration and service mesh enforcing mTLS and secure container communication.
* Go (Core Telehealth) & Python/FastAPI (AI Inference): High-performance microservices for backend logic and AI processing.
* HL7 FHIR & national e-prescription standards: Interoperability protocols for US and EU pharmacy integration.
* Google Cloud Operations Suite & Cloud Storage: Region-partitioned logging and secure audit storage.

## Rationale
The architecture strictly segregates workloads into regional GCP deployments to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA data residency constraints. Resilient edge caching, gRPC protocols, and mediasoup SFUs support low-bandwidth rural connections without compromising regulatory compliance or audit traceability.

Client Applications.analysis:
## Overview
Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance (GDPR/HIPAA/EU MDR), and high availability over unstable connections.

## Key Elements
* Patients and Clinicians (EU & US)
* Client Applications (Flutter / Web)
* UI Layer
* Local State & Storage Manager (Hive / SQLite with SQLCipher)
* Network & Sync Engine
* WebRTC Client SDK
* Localization & Accessibility Engine
* API Gateway (Envoy / Google Cloud Endpoints)
* Containerized SFUs (mediasoup)

## Relationships
* Patients and Clinicians -> Client Applications: Accesses platform capabilities [HTTPS / WebRTC]
* UI Layer -> API Gateway: Sends structured API requests [gRPC-Web / HTTPS]
* Network & Sync Engine -> API Gateway: Communicates with dynamic region endpoints [gRPC-Web / HTTPS with Certificate Pinning]
* WebRTC Client SDK -> Containerized SFUs (mediasoup): Streams video and audio [ICE / DTLS / SRTP]
* UI Layer -> Local State & Storage Manager: Reads and writes cached data [Encrypted Local I/O]

## Technology Stack
* Flutter / Web: Maximizes cross-platform reach for mobile and browser users while optimizing development costs.
* Hive / SQLite with SQLCipher: Secures cached PHI and consent preferences at rest using device-derived encryption keys.
* mediasoup SFU: Enables scalable, low-latency video consultations with adaptive codecs for connections below 300 kbit/s.
* OpenTelemetry & Crashlytics: Provides client-side observability with on-device PII/PHI scrubbing for telemetry data.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures regional compliance and robust offline resilience by combining encrypted local storage with dynamic jurisdiction routing. It maintains secure, low-bandwidth video sessions and traceable AI interactions to satisfy stringent healthcare regulations in both the EU and US.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. The system enforces strict regional data residency and compliance using GCP and cloud-native microservices.

## Key Elements
- Client Applications (Flutter / Web)
- GCP External HTTP(S) Load Balancer
- API Gateway (Envoy / Google Cloud Endpoints)
- Core Telehealth Service (Go)
- AI Inference Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Interoperability Service (Java / Spring Boot)
- Containerized SFUs (mediasoup)
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) with Istio mTLS mesh
- Regionalized Redis Caches

## Relationships
- Client Applications -> GCP External HTTP(S) Load Balancer: HTTPS / gRPC [TLS 1.3]
- GCP External HTTP(S) Load Balancer -> API Gateway: HTTPS / gRPC
- API Gateway -> Core Telehealth Service: gRPC over Istio mTLS mesh
- API Gateway -> AI Inference Service: gRPC over Istio mTLS mesh
- API Gateway -> Interoperability Service: gRPC over Istio mTLS mesh
- API Gateway -> Containerized SFUs: gRPC over Istio mTLS mesh

## Technology Stack
- GCP Cloud Load Balancing: Handles global geo-routing and region enforcement at the network edge.
- Envoy Proxy: Powers the API Gateway for TLS termination, routing, rate limiting, and resilience.
- Istio Service Mesh: Secures microservice communication with mTLS and SPIFFE/SPIRE identity propagation.
- Redis: Region-local caching for distributed rate limiting without cross-region dependencies.
- Prometheus & Cloud Trace: Observability, distributed tracing, and metric scraping for connection stability.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regional data separation required by GDPR and HIPAA by utilizing region-isolated infrastructure. Envoy proxy integration ensures stable communication for rural, low-bandwidth users while protecting backend AI and core services from abuse.

Core Telehealth Service.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency and compliance using Google Cloud Platform.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Clinic Administrators and Support Staff
- Flutter / Web Client Applications
- API Gateway (Envoy / Google Cloud Endpoints)
- Core Telehealth Service (Go container in GKE) decomposed into:
  - Consultation & Scheduling Component
  - Consent & Audit Engine
  - Data Residency Proxy
  - Prescription & Interoperability Orchestrator
- AI Inference Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Interoperability Service (Java / Spring Boot)
- Containerized SFUs (mediasoup)
- Regional PostgreSQL Databases with CMEK and Field-Level Encryption
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` managed via ArgoCD

## Relationships
- Client Applications -> API Gateway: Routes requests [HTTPS / WSS]
- API Gateway -> Core Telehealth Service: Routes core business requests [gRPC over Istio mTLS mesh]
- Core Telehealth Service components -> Regional PostgreSQL Databases: Persists and retrieves encrypted data [CMEK and FLE encrypted connections]
- Prescription & Interoperability Orchestrator -> Interoperability Service: Sends prescription data [gRPC over Istio mTLS]
- Internal Go components: Communicate via in-process Go function calls using shared-nothing in-memory state

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high performance and low-latency consultation workflows in the core service
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Dual-region orchestration (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`) ensuring data residency
- PostgreSQL: Regional databases with CMEK and Field-Level Encryption for PHI/PII protection
- Istio: Service mesh providing mTLS, circuit breaking, and traffic management
- ArgoCD: Regional continuous deployment preventing configuration drift
- GCP Secret Manager: Secure runtime injection of database credentials and signing secrets

## Rationale
The architecture strictly separates regional data environments to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA data residency constraints. Go-based micro-components on GKE optimize concurrency and support graceful degradation for rural patients with unstable internet connections.

AI Inference Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It ensures strict regional data residency, HIPAA/GDPR compliance, and high availability in rural environments.]

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Client Applications (Flutter / Web)
- API Gateway (Envoy / Google Cloud Endpoints)
- Core Telehealth Service (Go)
- AI Inference Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Interoperability Service (Java / Spring Boot)
- Containerized SFUs (mediasoup)
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`
- PostgreSQL Databases with CMEK and Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ)

## Relationships
- Client Applications -> API Gateway: Accesses platform features [HTTPS / gRPC]
- API Gateway -> AI Inference Service: Routes AI symptom check requests [gRPC over Istio mTLS mesh]
- AI Inference Service -> PostgreSQL Databases: Persists and retrieves encrypted audit/inference data [CMEK encrypted connection]
- GKE GPU Node Pools -> Cloud Storage Buckets: Pulls region-locked model weights [VPC Service Controls]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Multi-region target cloud ensuring regional compliance
- Python / FastAPI: Core framework for the AI Inference Service
- ONNX Runtime / PyTorch: Localized model execution engines
- spaCy / Regex: Synchronous safety guardrail and keyword filtering
- GCP Confidential VMs (AMD SEV-SNP): Protects in-memory data during GPU inference

## Rationale
[This architecture enforces regional data segregation and end-to-end encryption to satisfy strict HIPAA, GDPR, and EU MDR compliance mandates. Decoupled async audit pipelines and CPU/GPU isolation ensure high availability, audit traceability, and resilience for rural users.]

Interoperability Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It enforces strict regional data residency and interoperates with regional pharmacy systems.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Client Applications (Flutter / Web)
- API Gateway (Envoy / Google Cloud Endpoints)
- Core Telehealth Service (Go)
- AI Inference Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Interoperability Service (Java / Spring Boot) with internal components: FHIR Translation Engine, EU Gateway Adapter Module, Consent & Policy Enforcement Interceptor, and Async Dispatch & DLQ Manager
- Containerized SFUs (mediasoup)
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) in GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`) with Istio service mesh
- GCP Pub/Sub and Cloud KMS (CMEK)
- External National E-Prescription Gateways (EU) & US Pharmacy Systems

## Relationships
- Client Applications -> API Gateway: Accesses platform features [HTTPS / gRPC]
- API Gateway -> Interoperability Service: Routes interoperability and prescription requests [gRPC over Istio mTLS mesh]
- Interoperability Service (Consent Interceptor) -> FHIR Translation Engine & EU Gateway Adapter: Dispatches validated payloads [Spring Application Events]
- Interoperability Service -> External Gateways: Transmits prescription data [HTTPS / Mutual TLS]
- Interoperability Service -> GCP Pub/Sub: Persists unrecoverable payloads to Dead-Letter Queues [gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- Java / Spring Boot: Chosen for the Interoperability Service to leverage its enterprise ecosystem for complex regional data formats.
- GCP GKE & Istio: Deployed across dual regions (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`) with egress gateways to strictly enforce data residency and regional isolation.
- GCP Pub/Sub & Resilience4j: Implements persistent dead-letter queues and circuit breakers to handle transient failures from external gateways.
- GCP Secret Manager & Cloud KMS (CMEK): Secures external API keys, mTLS certificates, and encrypts DLQ payloads at rest per region.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict regulatory compliance with GDPR and HIPAA by enforcing regional data residency and robust consent validation. Furthermore, it guarantees clinical continuity and accountability through resilient asynchronous queuing and distributed tracing.

Containerized SFUs.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients on GCP. Containerized Selective Forwarding Units (SFUs) ensure real-time, low-bandwidth video communication while strictly enforcing regional data residency.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU & US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster spanning `europe-west3` and `us-central1`
- Containerized SFUs container (`mediasoup`)
- Signaling & Room Manager (Node.js/TypeScript)
- Media Router Worker & Bandwidth Adaptation Engine (C++)
- Core Telehealth Service (Go)

## Relationships
- Client Applications -> Containerized SFUs: WebRTC (ICE/DTLS/SRTP) for media streams and WebSockets (WSS) for signaling
- Signaling & Room Manager -> Core Telehealth Service: gRPC over Istio mTLS mesh for peer authorization, audit logging, and room state
- Signaling & Room Manager -> Media Router Worker: Local Unix sockets for inter-process communication (IPC)

## Technology Stack
- mediasoup / C++: High-performance WebRTC media routing and simulcast/SVC stream adaptation for bandwidth resilience (<300 kbit/s)
- Node.js/TypeScript: Signaling, room management, and worker lifecycle control
- GCP (GKE): Container orchestration with regional node affinity to enforce data residency
- Istio mTLS / gRPC: Secure service-to-service communication and control plane encryption
- tmpfs (RAM-backed emptyDir): Ephemeral memory isolation to prevent local disk persistence of media buffers

## Rationale
GKE regional node affinity guarantees that EU and US health data remain in their respective jurisdictions to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA. Containerized mediasoup SFUs with built-in simulcast and tmpfs isolation deliver low-bandwidth video resilience and zero-retention PHI security.

Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency and compliance using a multi-tenant cloud architecture.

## Key Elements
* Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE Standard) in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`
* Ingress Controller & API Gateway Pods (Envoy / Istio Ingress)
* Workload Pods (Go, Python, Java runtimes)
* Policy & Admission Controller (OPA Gatekeeper / Kubernetes ValidatingWebhook)
* Cluster Autoscaler & Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (Kubernetes HPA)
* Runtime Security Component (Falco DaemonSet)
* OpenTelemetry Collectors (DaemonSet)
* Secret Store CSI Driver (Google Secret Manager / HashiCorp Vault)

## Relationships
* External clients connect to Ingress Controller via HTTPS/WSS
* GKE control plane communicates with worker nodes via Kubernetes API over TLS 1.3
* Internal microservices communicate via gRPC/mTLS over Istio service mesh
* Telemetry streams from OpenTelemetry DaemonSet to Cloud Logging via gRPC

## Technology Stack
* Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE Standard): Mandated for precise node-level tuning of memory-intensive media SFUs and AI inference pods
* Istio Service Mesh & Envoy: Enforces mTLS, authorization policies, and geo-routing rules
* OPA Gatekeeper: Programmatically enforces regional data residency constraints
* Falco & Cilium CNI: Provides runtime kernel monitoring and layer-3/4 network policy enforcement
* Google Cloud KMS & Binary Authorization: Secures AI model traceability for EU MDR compliance

## Rationale
GKE Standard with regional multi-tenancy enforces strict GDPR and HIPAA data residency boundaries. Automated autoscaling and strict resource quotas ensure high availability and continuous degraded-mode video consultations over unstable rural connections.

PostgreSQL Databases.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. Its architecture enforces strict regional data isolation to comply with GDPR and HIPAA mandates.

## Key Elements
- PostgreSQL Databases (Region-isolated instances in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`)
- Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (Relational storage engine)
- Cloud SQL Auth Proxy (Sidecar proxy for secure connections)
- PgBouncer (Connection pooler)
- Core Telehealth Service
- AI Inference Service
- Schemas (`core_domain`, `consent_ledger`, `ai_audit`)

## Relationships
- Core Telehealth Service -> PostgreSQL Databases: Persists and retrieves patient and consultation data via TCP port 5432 using TLS 1.3 and Cloud SQL Auth Proxy
- AI Inference Service -> PostgreSQL Databases: Stores symptom checker inputs, outputs, and model versions via TCP port 5432 using TLS 1.3 and Cloud SQL Auth Proxy

## Technology Stack
- Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: Managed relational database ensuring enterprise availability and point-in-time recovery
- Cloud SQL Auth Proxy & mTLS: Secures database transport without static passwords
- PostgreSQL `pgaudit`: Provides comprehensive audit logging for GDPR and HIPAA compliance
- GCP Cloud KMS: Supplies Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) for data-at-rest encryption

## Rationale
Region-isolated database instances guarantee that EU health data remains in `europe-west3` and US data in `us-central1`. Immutable schemas and strict IAM controls fulfill regional privacy regulations and AI traceability mandates.
